- Country folders are navigation aids rather than political or custody determinations. Crimea, Sevastopol and other Ukrainian regions remain cross-referenced by their Ukrainian geographic entries; source authorities may classify territories differently.
- The Russian browse list uses 83 non-overlapping regional entries plus cross-border references, rather than silently duplicating disputed territories under competing administrative claims.
- USSR republic names and borders changed before 1991; the 15-country index does not represent every historical Soviet administrative arrangement.
- Azerbaijan, Georgia and Latvia currently include archive service areas from retrieved institutional directories; these must not be presented as exhaustive current civil-administrative district lists.

Completion requires a dated official list, branch reconciliation, transfer review and a written explanation. A failed connection never removes an institution.
